ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution with a predominant low-intensity (black) base covering approximately 75-80% of the surface, punctuated by high-intensity (white) localized pixel clusters and linear formations.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Primary dark pigmentation layer overlaid with a complex network of high-intensity white geometric blobs. These include circular constellations distributed randomly and dense, unaligned linear streaks concentrated heavily in the central and right-central fluke regions.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Distinct V-shaped central depression with a calculated internal angle of approximately 40-45 degrees relative to the horizontal fluke axis.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serration profile along the trailing edge, characterized by jagged pixel peaks and valleys ranging from 5 to 15 pixels in depth, isolated clearly against the water/sky background.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Bilateral convex curvature extending from the median notch toward the distal tips, exhibiting a slight downward (posterior) sweep before tapering to points.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple high-intensity circular and elliptical pixel clusters (approximately 10-25 pixels in diameter) visible across both lobes, with higher density observed on the distal tips.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Extensive network of white, non-parallel linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) ranging from 20 to 150 pixels in length, most prominent on the right lobe where they intersect at various angles.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extreme density of white linear scarring and circular lesions (consistent with rake marks and barnacle scars) covering nearly the entire visible surface of both fluke lobes.
other_distinctive_markers: The intersection density of linear abrasions on the right lobe creates a unique 'cross-hatched' pixel pattern not commonly seen in standard pigmentation.
